page_placements.theme: Interpretability scores and explanations can be inflated, manipulated or unreliable

record.file_problem: none; the full LessWrong post is present, though it points to a separate full report.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports its own evaluations of sparse-autoencoder feature explanations, not neuron poles or neuron explanations. Those results do not test the listed neuron claims.
record.gate_note: The post evaluates explanations of Gemma-2 SAE features. Its explanation failures and Detection/Fuzz scores are relevant to interpretability but concern SAE features, not individual neurons or neuron poles. The post also mentions an optimal steering strength around 2–3 and a 50% activation rate; these are tool-tuning details, not results about the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The post evaluates explanations of Gemma-2-2B SAE latents (Gemma Scope, layer 20), not individual neurons or neuron poles. None of its results measure what V1–V7 name. It does not use or cite the original sources. Its SAE-feature findings parallel V6 and V7 only by analogy and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find that the agent matches Delphi (81.6% vs 83.8%) but does not beat it. Human experts, whose explanations better satisfied the authors' criteria, scored lower (67.6% full average; 58% Detection). They take this as weak evidence of a score ceiling set by SAE feature quality (splitting, absorption, polysemanticity), and conclude that current scorers reward scorer-friendly explanations.
record.recipe_differences: The post studies SAE-feature explanations using Delphi-style Detection/Fuzz scoring, a tool-augmented explanation agent, and human explanations. It does not audit neuron poles or use the original neuron-pole method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported scores vary by SAE-feature concentration class; the authors say score ceilings fall for more diffuse features. They also report differing performance across explanation methods and metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 50-latent Gemma Scope sample, 19 Delphi explanations (38%) failed the authors' criteria. On 27 latents, Detection/Fuzz scores were: Delphi 85.1/78.8, agent 80.9/76.5, human 58.0/58.9. About 15% of latents are output-centric and all automated methods misexplain them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-example-based explanations of SAE latents often fail quality criteria, and LLM scorers reward simple explanations over more accurate qualified ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Top activations look clean, but lower-quantile activations (>98% of activations) are noisier. Score ceilings fall from 91.6% for NARROW latents to 76.7% for DIFFUSE latents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For SAE latents, explanations fitted to top activating examples overstate how cleanly the unit's full activation distribution is explained. This is an SAE analogue of V6.

record.problems: The reported experiments concern SAE features in one Gemma-2 model and one SAE layer, not neurons. The aggregate scoring sample is 27 latents; the initial manual audit covers 50 features. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the authors note that the scoring methods can reward scorer-friendly explanations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes omitted. Tool-strength tuning details and individual feature examples are not recorded as rows because they do not measure a listed neuron-claim version.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles.
No cross-model or scale comparison of neuron shares.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No comparison of neuron interpretability across architectures or tools.
Explanation-versus-activation mismatch is shown for SAE latents only, not neurons.
Simulation-style detection/fuzz scoring is applied to SAE latents only, not neurons.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern SAE latents, so no version verdicts are given. The post is a summary pointing to a fuller report. Samples are small (27 and 50 latents), with one SAE, one layer, and a single scorer and explainer model (Claude Haiku 4.5). No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or their job counts.
No comparison of neuron-pole shares across models, architectures, or scales.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or pose/recursive-generalization test.
No test of neuron interpretability across architectures, regularization, tools, or vision-model estimates.
No attribution-graph test of whether a model's own neurons suffice as circuit units.
The post tests SAE-feature explanations against activations, not explanations of neurons.
Automated scores are reported for SAE-feature explanations, not neuron explanations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The post covers explanations from activating examples and LLM-scorer limits for SAE features, which is analogous to V6/V7. It runs no neuron tests and does not cite the originals, so cites_only does not fit.

tranche.reason: The post explains and scores Gemma-2-2B SAE latents (Gemma Scope, layer 20), not neurons or neuron poles. It neither tests nor uses the claim, and SAE latents are a different construct from neurons.

source_check.notes: All rows are SAE latents of Gemma-2-2B (Gemma Scope 16k, layer 20). Claude Haiku 4.5 wrote and scored all explanations, so none of the rows bear on neuron-pole versions V1-V7. Table 2 covers n=27 latents. The 38% failure audit covers the first 50 features against the authors' own 5 criteria.

statements.problem: All numbers match the text: 19/50 (38%) Delphi explanations failed (l.55), and Table 2 (n=27) Detection/Fuzz is 85.1/78.8 Delphi, 80.9/76.5 Agent and 58.0/58.9 Human. The 15% figure is about 15% of the features the authors examined (l.303). The scorer point is correctly labelled as the authors' claim.
